# Behavioral Requirements — Linux virtio driver subsystem

> Generated by [Quality Playbook](https://github.com/andrewstellman/quality-playbook) v1.6.0 — Andrew Stellman
> Date: 2026-07-19 · Project: linux-virtio (sparse kernel subsystem checkout @ bfe62a454542)

Version: v1.0
Generated: 2026-07-19

## Project overview

This subsystem is the guest-side of Linux's virtio paravirtualized I/O. A transport-abstraction
core (`virtio.c`, `virtio_ring.c`) defines the device lifecycle — probe, feature negotiation,
virtqueue setup, descriptor add/get, interrupt dispatch — and four transport backends bind that
lifecycle to a concrete bus: PCI-modern (`virtio_pci_modern.c`), PCI-legacy
(`virtio_pci_legacy.c`), MMIO (`virtio_mmio.c`), and vDPA (`virtio_vdpa.c`). Each transport
supplies a `config_ops` vtable; the core calls through it. The actors are the guest driver
(this code) and a hypervisor-side device backend (QEMU, vhost, or vDPA hardware) on the other
side of the virtqueue, plus the platform DMA/IOMMU and PCI/MMIO buses.

The central correctness property of this subsystem is **cross-transport contract consistency**:
four parallel implementations of the same lifecycle operations (`finalize_features`, `reset`,
the interrupt handler, `get_features`) must each honor the same spec contracts from
`reference_docs/virtio-spec-behavioral-contracts.md` (§1 feature negotiation, §5 reset, the
interrupt and barrier sections). The most dangerous bug class — and the one Phase 1 found
repeatedly — is a shared filter (`vring_transport_features`) that silently drops feature bits it
does not enumerate, where only one of four transports compensates. Because this is a Tier-3
(code-is-the-spec) run with a Tier-4 behavioral-contracts doc and no `cite/` corpus, every
requirement below is `inferred` or `Tier-4`; there are no Tier 1/2 formal-spec REQs.

The product requirements are grouped into three functional sections: **Feature negotiation** (the
transport-bit whitelist and its compensation grid — the highest-yield surface), **Cross-transport
lifecycle parity** (device reset and interrupt dispatch, the two lifecycle operations where a
single spec contract is implemented four times), and **Virtqueue ring invariants** (the
ownership-encoding and memory-ordering properties of the ring itself). The playbook's own
artifact-layout invariants — which are not requirements of the audited system — are rendered
separately in `quality/RUN_CONTRACT.md`.

**Coverage and known gaps.** This derivation covered the transport-abstraction core
(`virtio.c`, `virtio_ring.c`) and all four transport backends at the level of the shared
lifecycle contracts: feature negotiation and the transport-bit whitelist, device reset, interrupt
dispatch, and the packed/split ring publication invariants. Those surfaces were read closely and
are where every requirement below comes from. The derivation knowingly did **not** cover: the
per-device drivers that sit above this layer — and this is the largest uncovered surface that is
actually **in** the checkout. `virtio_balloon.c`, `virtio_mem.c`, `virtio_input.c`,
`virtio_dma_buf.c` and the `virtio_rtc_*.c` family are all present in `drivers/virtio/` and none
of them is referenced by any requirement below; nothing here constrains how they consume the
contracts this document specifies. (The more familiar per-device drivers — virtio-net, -blk,
-scsi — live outside `drivers/virtio/` and are genuinely outside the checkout, which is a
different and weaker claim.) Also uncovered: the DMA/IOMMU mapping
and unmapping paths in `virtio_ring.c`, which were skimmed for barrier placement only and never
turned into REQs; the admin-virtqueue and SR-IOV command surfaces, which are referenced by
feature bits 37 and 41 but whose command handling was not read; suspend/resume and hot-unplug
lifecycle paths; and the vDPA backend contract itself, which lives behind `vdpa_*` calls in code
outside this checkout and is therefore out of reach. Coverage is also tier-limited: with no
`reference_docs/cite/` corpus, no requirement here can be traced to a formal external
specification — the strongest available basis is the Tier-4 behavioral-contracts document, and
the rest is inferred from the source. A reader should treat the ring-invariant section
(REQ-007..REQ-009) as the thinnest: three REQs for the largest and most intricate file in the
subsystem.

## Actors and roles

The requirements below serve four distinct readers, and each section is written with one of them
in mind. Sections are ordered **user-facing → infrastructure**: feature negotiation is what a
device backend and a driver author interact with first, lifecycle parity is what a transport
maintainer owns, and the ring invariants are the internal machinery underneath both.

- **Guest driver author (virtio-net, -blk, -scsi, …).** Binds to a virtio device through the
  core. Cares that a feature bit the device offered actually survives negotiation and that a
  requested virtqueue size is honored or rejected — not silently truncated.
- **Transport maintainer (PCI-modern, PCI-legacy, MMIO, vDPA).** Owns one `config_ops` vtable and
  must implement the same lifecycle contract the other three implement. Every parity requirement
  in this document names the conformant reference transport so a maintainer can diff against it.
- **Device backend implementer (QEMU, vhost, vDPA hardware).** Sits on the far side of the
  virtqueue and observes the guest's negotiated feature set, status writes, and published ring
  indices. Depends on the guest honoring the ordering and acknowledgement contracts.
- **Kernel IRQ core and platform (DMA/IOMMU, PCI/MMIO buses).** Not a person, but a contract
  counterparty: it interprets a handler's `IRQ_HANDLED` / `IRQ_NONE` return and enforces the
  memory model that makes the barrier requirements load-bearing.

## Feature negotiation

Feature negotiation is the heart of this audit. The core preserves every device-offered transport
bit (`virtio.c:319-321`), then `vring_transport_features` (`virtio_ring.c:3505-3532`) runs a
closed-set whitelist that clears any transport bit it does not explicitly enumerate, and finally
each transport's `finalize_features` is expected to re-preserve the bits the whitelist could not
know about. The contract theme is therefore **a shared filter plus per-transport compensation**:
no single site can be judged correct on its own, because correctness is a property of the pair.
The asymmetry — modern PCI compensates, MMIO and vDPA do not, and bit 39 is compensated by
nobody — is the dominant defect vector in this subsystem.

### REQ-001: Transport feature-bit preservation across all non-legacy transports

- Tier: inferred — from source (compensation asymmetry across transports)
- References: drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_modern.c, drivers/virtio/virtio_mmio.c, drivers/virtio/virtio_vdpa.c
- Pattern: compensation
- Conditions of satisfaction:
  1. All non-legacy transports must preserve device-offered transport feature bits (28..41) that
     `vring_transport_features` cannot enumerate. Concretely: after `vring_transport_features(vdev)`
     runs, each non-legacy transport's `finalize_features` re-adds (via `__virtio_set_bit` or
     equivalent) every transport bit the device offered that the whitelist cleared, before
     writing/forwarding the negotiated feature set.
  2. PCI-modern's `vp_transport_features` (virtio_pci_modern.c:367-381) is the reference
     compensator: it re-adds SR_IOV(37, capability-guarded), RING_RESET(40), ADMIN_VQ(41).
  3. MMIO `vm_finalize_features` (virtio_mmio.c:109-132) must re-preserve RING_RESET(40) /
     ADMIN_VQ(41) / NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA(39) / SR_IOV(37) before writing
     `VIRTIO_MMIO_DRIVER_FEATURES`. It currently does not (candidate BUG).
  4. vDPA `virtio_vdpa_finalize_features` (virtio_vdpa.c:389-397) must re-preserve those bits
     before `vdpa_set_features`. It currently does not (candidate BUG).
  5. (Asymmetry: "modern PCI compensates via vp_transport_features; MMIO and vDPA rely entirely
     on vring_transport_features and compensate for nothing.")

### REQ-002: Whitelist enumeration or compensator coverage for every supported transport feature bit

- Tier: inferred — from source (closed-set enumeration vs authoritative header)
- References: drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c, include/uapi/linux/virtio_config.h, drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_modern.c
- Pattern: whitelist
- Conditions of satisfaction:
  1. `vring_transport_features` must enumerate — or the calling transport must compensate for —
     every transport feature bit any transport supports. Concretely: every transport bit in
     `[VIRTIO_TRANSPORT_F_START(28), VIRTIO_TRANSPORT_F_END(42))` (virtio_config.h:54-55) that any
     transport supports is either an explicit `case` label in `vring_transport_features`
     (virtio_ring.c:3511-3525) OR re-added by the calling transport's compensator.
  2. The mechanically-extracted case set (quality/mechanical/vring_transport_features_cases.txt)
     contains exactly the 8 labels: INDIRECT_DESC, EVENT_IDX, VERSION_1, ACCESS_PLATFORM,
     RING_PACKED, ORDER_PLATFORM, NOTIFICATION_DATA, IN_ORDER.
  3. Bits absent from the case set — SR_IOV(37), NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA(39), RING_RESET(40),
     ADMIN_VQ(41) — hit `default:` (virtio_ring.c:3527) and are cleared
     (`__virtio_clear_bit`, virtio_ring.c:3529); each must therefore be covered by a transport
     compensator. NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA(39) is covered by no compensator (candidate BUG).

### REQ-003: NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA(39) survival on any transport whose finalize validates it

- Tier: inferred — from source (compensator/validator disagreement)
- References: drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_modern.c
- Pattern: compensation
- Conditions of satisfaction:
  1. `vp_check_common_size` (virtio_pci_modern.c:405-417) validates the `queue_notify_data`
     config sizing when `VIRTIO_F_NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA` is set; this check is only meaningful if
     bit 39 can survive negotiation.
  2. `vp_transport_features` (virtio_pci_modern.c:367-381) must re-add NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA(39)
     after `vring_transport_features` clears it. It currently does not, so the validator at
     virtio_pci_modern.c:405-417 is dead and the `queue_notify_data` path is unreachable
     (candidate BUG).

### REQ-004: Negotiation acceptance confirmed for VERSION_1 devices and intentionally absent for legacy

- Tier: Tier-4 — behavioral-contracts.md §1
- References: drivers/virtio/virtio.c
- Conditions of satisfaction:
  1. `virtio_features_ok` (virtio.c:204-235) sets `VIRTIO_CONFIG_S_FEATURES_OK` (line 227),
     re-reads status (line 228), and returns -ENODEV if the bit did not stick (lines 229-232).
  2. For non-VERSION_1 (legacy) devices, `virtio_features_ok` early-returns 0 (lines 224-225)
     before touching FEATURES_OK — the legacy path has no acceptance confirmation by design
     ("no safe failure mechanism"). This is a documented intentional divergence, not a defect.

## Cross-transport lifecycle parity

Reset and interrupt dispatch are the two device-lifecycle operations where one spec contract is
implemented four times, once per transport, with no shared code to hold them together. The
contract theme is **parity against a named conformant reference**: for each operation exactly one
transport is the reference implementation, and every other transport's divergence from it is
either an intentional, documented exemption or a defect. Reset (§5) says write 0 to the device
status, then wait until a status read returns 0 before reinitializing; PCI-modern implements the
poll, MMIO omits it entirely, vDPA delegates to the backend, and PCI-legacy uses a single
flush-read that is arguably correct for pre-1.0 devices but undocumented as intentional.
Interrupt dispatch says a handler returns IRQ_HANDLED whenever it consumed a real interrupt;
MMIO is the reference and PCI discards `vp_config_changed`'s IRQ_HANDLED return, so a config-only
interrupt is reported to the kernel as spurious. Reviewing these two together is deliberate — the
failure shape is identical, and a reader who has internalized it in one operation spots it
immediately in the other.

### REQ-005: Device-reset write-0-then-wait-for-status-0 parity across transports

- Tier: Tier-4 — behavioral-contracts.md §5
- References: drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_modern.c, drivers/virtio/virtio_mmio.c, drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_legacy.c
- Pattern: parity
- Conditions of satisfaction:
  1. Every transport's device-reset path must satisfy the spec §5 "write 0 then wait for status
     read 0" contract, or document an intentional legacy exemption.
  2. PCI-modern `vp_reset` (virtio_pci_modern.c:546-565): writes 0 (line 552), then polls
     `while (vp_modern_get_status(mdev)) msleep(1);` (lines 558-559). CONFORMANT — reference.
  3. MMIO `vm_reset` (virtio_mmio.c:251-257): must wait for status read 0 after writing 0
     (line 256). It returns immediately with no poll loop (candidate BUG).
  4. vDPA `virtio_vdpa_reset` (virtio_vdpa.c:86-91): delegates to `vdpa_reset`; guest-side reinit
     must not assume synchronous completion (the backend owns the wait).
  5. PCI-legacy `vp_reset` (virtio_pci_legacy.c:93-103): single flush-read (no poll) is acceptable
     ONLY if documented as an intentional pre-1.0 exemption; an undocumented omission is a defect.

### REQ-006: IRQ_HANDLED return from every handler that serviced a config-change interrupt

- Tier: inferred — from source (dispatcher return-value divergence)
- References: drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_common.c, drivers/virtio/virtio_mmio.c, drivers/virtio/virtio_vdpa.c
- Pattern: parity
- Conditions of satisfaction:
  1. Every transport interrupt handler must return IRQ_HANDLED when it serviced a config-change
     interrupt, independent of vring activity. Concretely: when the handler services a
     config-change interrupt with no vring activity, it returns IRQ_HANDLED — never IRQ_NONE.
  2. MMIO `vm_interrupt` (virtio_mmio.c:285-307) is the reference: it sets `ret = IRQ_HANDLED` on
     the CONFIG bit (lines 296-299) and returns `ret` (line 306). CONFORMANT.
  3. PCI `vp_interrupt` (virtio_pci_common.c:106-124) calls `vp_config_changed` (lines 120-121)
     but discards its IRQ_HANDLED return (vp_config_changed returns IRQ_HANDLED at
     virtio_pci_common.c:79) and returns `vp_vring_interrupt(...)` (line 123), which returns
     IRQ_NONE when no vring callback fires (virtio_pci_common.c:97). So `isr ==
     VIRTIO_PCI_ISR_CONFIG` exactly returns IRQ_NONE (candidate BUG).

## Virtqueue ring invariants

The ring code maintains ownership and ordering invariants that are currently correct but
high-blast-radius: the packed-ring wrap counter and avail/used flags must toggle together, and
every descriptor write must be followed by a barrier before the publishing index update. The
contract theme is **single-site invariants with no cross-check** — unlike the parity sections
above, there is no second implementation to diff against, so a future edit that breaks one of
these corrupts the ring silently on weakly-ordered architectures. Driver-requested queue size
should also be bounded by the device maximum (spec §9).

### REQ-007: Packed-ring wrap-counter and avail/used descriptor flags toggle together on ring wrap

- Tier: inferred — from source (ownership-encoding invariant)
- References: drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c
- Conditions of satisfaction:
  1. On a packed-ring wrap, `avail_wrap_counter` is XOR-toggled AND both the AVAIL and USED
     descriptor flag bits in `avail_used_flags` are flipped in the same operation
     (virtio_ring.c packed wrap site ~1580-1583).
  2. No code path toggles the wrap counter without flipping the flags, or vice versa — doing so
     gives descriptors the wrong ownership encoding and the device reads stale/unowned
     descriptors.

### REQ-008: Descriptor writes ordered before the index update that publishes them

- Tier: Tier-4 — behavioral-contracts.md §6
- References: drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c
- Conditions of satisfaction:
  1. In both split and packed paths, each `avail`/`used` index update is preceded by the correct
     `virtio_wmb` / `virtio_store_mb` barrier (barrier sites include virtio_ring.c:756, 802, 939,
     964, 1111, 1569, 1743, 1901, 2085, 2125, 2184).
  2. A descriptor published without a preceding write barrier corrupts the ring on weakly-ordered
     architectures (ARM) while remaining invisible on x86.

### REQ-009: Driver-requested virtqueue size bounded by the device-advertised maximum

- Tier: Tier-4 — behavioral-contracts.md §9
- References: drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c
- Conditions of satisfaction:
  1. The virtqueue-creation path (`vring_create_virtqueue` family near virtio_ring.c:3505) rejects
     or clamps a requested size larger than the device-advertised `queue_size`/`num_max`.
  2. A driver that requests more descriptors than the device supports does not silently allocate a
     ring the device cannot service.

## Cross-cutting concerns

**Compensation grid.** The dominant architectural invariant is that any feature bit the shared
whitelist (`vring_transport_features`) clears must be re-preserved by every transport that
supports it. REQ-001, REQ-002, and REQ-003 form a grid: REQ-002 is the whitelist's closed set,
REQ-001 is per-transport compensation, REQ-003 is the single-bit (NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA) case where
the validator and the compensator disagree. A reviewer must read these three together — a bit can
be "covered" by REQ-002's compensator clause yet still dropped because the specific transport
(REQ-001) omits it.

**Cross-transport parity.** REQ-005 (reset) and REQ-006 (interrupt return value) are parity
requirements: a single spec contract that all transports must satisfy identically, with one
transport serving as the conformant reference (PCI-modern for reset, MMIO for interrupt return).
The bug is always the transport that diverges from the reference.

**Bit-width boundary.** Legacy (PCI-legacy) is 32-bit-only; transport bits 37-41 are out of its
range. REQ-001's compensation requirement therefore explicitly exempts legacy, and REQ-004
documents that legacy intentionally skips FEATURES_OK confirmation. Any reviewer treating legacy
as "missing compensation" has misread the boundary.

**Tier discipline.** No requirement in this document is Tier 1/2 (formal external spec) — the run
has no `reference_docs/cite/` corpus. Every REQ is `inferred` (from source) or `Tier-4` (the
behavioral-contracts doc). Consequently `citation_semantic_check.json` is not required this run.

## Use cases

The use cases below expand each cross-transport requirement into one scenario per transport site,
so that a reviewer can check the contract against a concrete code path rather than in the
abstract. Requirements whose sites are genuinely parallel — REQ-001 (feature-bit preservation),
REQ-005 (reset), REQ-006 (interrupt return) — get one use case per transport. REQ-002 covers a
header-and-switch surface whose sites are not parallel, so it gets a single umbrella use case.

### UC-1.a: Transport-bit preservation on PCI-modern
- Actor: virtio_pci_modern driver, device backend
- Preconditions: device advertises RING_RESET(40) / ADMIN_VQ(41) / SR_IOV(37)
- Steps: `vp_finalize_features` → `vring_transport_features` clears the bits →
  `vp_transport_features` (virtio_pci_modern.c:367-381) re-adds them
- Postconditions: bits survive into `vp_modern_set_extended_features` (NOTE: bit 39 NOT re-added —
  see UC-5 / REQ-003)

### UC-1.b: Transport-bit preservation on MMIO
- Actor: virtio_mmio driver, device backend
- Preconditions: MMIO device advertises RING_RESET(40)
- Steps: `vm_finalize_features` → `vring_transport_features` clears bit → NO re-add → write to
  `VIRTIO_MMIO_DRIVER_FEATURES`
- Postconditions: bit MUST survive but currently does not (candidate BUG)

### UC-1.c: Transport-bit preservation on vDPA
- Actor: virtio_vdpa driver, vDPA backend
- Preconditions: vDPA backend advertises RING_RESET(40)
- Steps: `virtio_vdpa_finalize_features` → `vring_transport_features` clears →
  `vdpa_set_features` forwards stripped set
- Postconditions: bit MUST survive to set_features but currently does not (candidate BUG)

### UC-2: Transport feature-bit whitelist completeness
- Actor: virtio_ring core, all transports
- Preconditions: device offers any bit in [28,42)
- Steps: `vring_transport_features` switch decides survival; the calling transport compensates for
  cleared bits
- Postconditions: every transport-supported bit is enumerated or compensated

### UC-3.a: Reset wait-for-zero on PCI-modern
- Actor: virtio_pci_modern driver, device
- Preconditions: driver initiates reset by writing 0 to device status
- Steps: write 0 (virtio_pci_modern.c:552) → poll `while get_status` (lines 558-559)
- Postconditions: status reads 0 before reinit — CONFORMANT

### UC-3.b: Reset wait-for-zero on MMIO
- Actor: virtio_mmio driver, device
- Preconditions: driver initiates reset by writing 0 to `VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS`
- Steps: write 0 (virtio_mmio.c:256) → (no wait)
- Postconditions: status MUST read 0 before reinit; MMIO currently returns immediately
  (candidate BUG)

### UC-3.c: Reset wait-for-zero on PCI-legacy
- Actor: virtio_pci_legacy driver, pre-1.0 device
- Preconditions: driver initiates reset by writing 0 to the legacy status port
- Steps: write 0 (virtio_pci_legacy.c:97) → single flush-read
- Postconditions: acceptable only if documented as an intentional pre-1.0 exemption

### UC-4.a: Config-interrupt return value on PCI
- Actor: virtio_pci interrupt handler, kernel IRQ core
- Preconditions: a config-change interrupt fires with no vring activity (isr ==
  VIRTIO_PCI_ISR_CONFIG)
- Steps: `vp_interrupt` reads ISR, calls `vp_config_changed` (discarding its return), returns
  `vp_vring_interrupt` result
- Postconditions: handler should return IRQ_HANDLED; currently returns IRQ_NONE (candidate BUG)

### UC-4.b: Config-interrupt return value on MMIO
- Actor: virtio_mmio interrupt handler, kernel IRQ core
- Preconditions: a config-change interrupt fires with no vring activity (status & INT_CONFIG)
- Steps: `vm_interrupt` sets `ret = IRQ_HANDLED` on CONFIG (lines 296-299), returns `ret`
- Postconditions: handler returns IRQ_HANDLED — CONFORMANT (reference for REQ-006)

### UC-4.c: Config-interrupt return value on vDPA
- Actor: virtio_vdpa interrupt path, kernel IRQ core
- Preconditions: a config-change notification reaches the vDPA config callback
- Steps: vDPA config-change callback services the change
- Postconditions: the config-change is acknowledged as handled (the vDPA path routes config
  changes through `virtio_config_changed`)

### UC-5: NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA survival on PCI-modern
- Actor: virtio_pci_modern driver, modern device with queue_notify_data
- Preconditions: modern device advertises NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA(39)
- Steps: `vp_finalize_features` → `vring_transport_features` clears bit 39 →
  `vp_transport_features` does NOT re-add it → `vp_check_common_size` validates a bit that is
  already cleared
- Postconditions: bit 39 MUST survive for the validator and the `queue_notify_data` path to be
  reachable; currently it does not (candidate BUG)
